subject: Astronomy & Space
title: The Pillars of Creation
description: One-minute skill: The Pillars of Creation.

hook.text: The Pillars of Creation are towering columns of gas and dust inside the Eagle Nebula—one of astronomy's most famous images.

buildup.text: Hubble captured them in 1995. The tallest pillar is about 5 light-years tall—larger than the distance to the nearest star.

discovery.text: Young stars form inside the pillar tips. Radiation from nearby massive stars slowly erodes the columns from outside.

twist.text: Infrared images show the pillars are transparent at longer wavelengths. Baby stars glow through the dust like hidden jewels.

climax.text: JWST re-imaged the Pillars in 2022 with stunning infrared detail, revealing newborn stars invisible to Hubble.

punchline.text: Columns of gas five light-years tall. Stars are being born inside them right now.

quiz.question: What is happening inside the Pillars of Creation?
options: New stars are forming inside the dense gas while radiation from nearby stars erodes the pillars
Ancient stars are dying and collapsing into black holes
Dark matter is accumulating and will eventually form a new galaxy

details.summary: The Pillars of Creation are towering columns of interstellar gas and dust in the Eagle Nebula (M16), about 6,500 light-years from Earth. Made famous by a 1995 Hubble image, these pillars are being sculpted by ultraviolet radiation from nearby stars while simultaneously forming new stars within…
details.whyItMatters: The Pillars became the most iconic space image ever taken, inspiring public interest in astronomy. They showcase the dynamic interplay of star formation and destruction happening within nebulae.
takeaways: Towering gas and dust columns in the Eagle Nebula
Being simultaneously eroded and forming new stars
Made famous by the iconic 1995 Hubble image

faq.question: Do the Pillars of Creation still exist?
faq.answer: Likely yes, though a nearby supernova may have sent a shock wave that could destroy them. Since the Pillars are 6,500 light-years away, we see them as they were 6,500 years ago. Evidence of a possible destructive shock is debated, but the Pillars may persist for another 100,000 years.

faq.question: How big are the Pillars of Creation?
faq.answer: The tallest pillar extends about 4-5 light-years — roughly the distance from the Sun to the nearest star. Each pillar's width is about 1 light-year. Dense knots at the tips (EGGs — evaporating gaseous globules) are roughly the size of our solar system and may contain forming stars.
